"} EXACT PASSAGE REFERENCES: [P001] Gemini comes to Windows with an Alt + Space shortcut [P002] Google announced the Windows app on September 10; it is available globally for Windows 10 and 11. Press Alt + Space to open it beside the app you are using. It brings Gemini’s quick answers, drafting and brainstorming into a window beside an active app. [P003] That is the practical difference from the browser: the shortcut and window are closer to the task. If you are revising a school-volunteer email, you could paste the draft and ask for a warmer version that keeps the date and request unchanged. You still check it before sending. [P004] Think of browser Gemini and the Windows app as two doors into the same shop. The new door may save a few steps; it does not make Gemini a different kind of tool. [P005] Google lists Windows 10 or later, 8 GB of RAM, 200 MB of disk space and internet access. You also need a personal Google Account, or a work or school account with Gemini enabled by its administrator. On a managed account, that administrator controls availability. [P006] You can choose to upload an image or connect Google apps such as Gmail and Drive. Read what you are connecting and only share material you are comfortable using with the service. [P007] If browser Gemini already suits you, nothing requires a switch. Try the app if the shortcut would make a small drafting or brainstorming task easier to start. Before you do, check the account you are using and decide what information you want to upload or connect. [P008] “Gemini on Windows is mostly a faster doorway: Alt + Space opens it beside what you are doing. It is not proof that Gemini can automatically see your screen, files or every app.” [P009] A desktop app changes the route into a tool. It does not erase account controls, feature limits or the need to decide what information to share.
